assessments.reasoning: For authenticity, publisher_live is Creative Commons' own /publicdomain/zero/1.0/legalcode.txt. For integrity, its full digest matches the scoped revision and publisher_pin, and [5884,6024) matches the cited clause digest. For relevance, section 4(a) expressly addresses both classes of rights. For interpretation, “licensed or otherwise affected” closes the fallback-license reading as well as the waiver reading. For applicability, “held by Affirmer” limits the holder, and the Statement of Purpose identifies the Affirmer as the person applying CC0 to the Work. For contradiction, sections 2 and 3 are confined to Copyright and Related Rights, section 1(iv) preserves the 4(a) limitation, and section 4(c) disclaims responsibility for clearing others' rights.

challenge.method: Tested section 2's broad waiver and section 3's fallback license separately against section 4(a). Checked section 1(iv) for overlapping unfair-competition rights and section 4(c) for the treatment of other rights holders.
challenge.results: Section 2 waives the Affirmer's Copyright and Related Rights to the extent permitted by law. Section 3 licenses that same class of rights to the extent the waiver is judged ineffective, and its residual nonassertion language also concerns that class. Section 4(a) expressly excludes both waiver and licensing of the Affirmer's patent and trademark rights. Section 1(iv) expressly defers to 4(a). Section 4(c) leaves third-party clearance a separate matter.

limitations: The finding concerns the instrument's stated effect on rights held by the Affirmer. Ownership, separate grants, defenses and permissions from other rights holders require separate evidence.
reasoning: When an Affirmer applies this edition to a Work, section 4(a) expressly excludes patent and trademark rights “held by Affirmer” from waiver, surrender, licensing and any other effect of the document. Its wording reaches both the dedication and the fallback.
